name: POST /api/leadflow/leads/:id/breach - record a breach with its mandatory cause and customer recovery
description:
Records an SLA breach. BOTH THE REASON AND THE RECOVERY ARE MANDATORY (12ce1f53-ba07-4f62-a2ac-a0b065100b28#AC2), enforced in the handler and again by a CHECK constraint so no writer can store one without the other.

WHY BOTH. A breach with no cause is a number on a report that teaches nobody anything, and the report exists to change what happens next. A cause with no recovery records what went wrong internally without recording what was actually done FOR THE CUSTOMER, which is the half SOP §04 cares about - the customer does not benefit from an explanation they never receive.

ONE BREACH PER LEAD, enforced by a UNIQUE constraint. A lead does not breach the same 30-minute clock twice, and a second call returns the existing record with already_recorded true rather than creating a duplicate that would double-count every attainment figure.

THE SYSTEMIC FLAG SEPARATES COACHING FROM INCIDENT RESPONSE. A breach caused by a broken workflow is not a rep who needs a conversation, and marking it opens a management incident instead.

QA: depends on register and login.

testCases.name: Recording a breach against an unknown lead is refused

payload.recovery_action: {{static:Called the customer at 10:05 and apologised, booked a survey}}

testCases.name: NEGATIVE: a breach with no reason code is refused
NEGATIVE: a breach with no recovery action is refused
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all
NEGATIVE: a bearer token that does not verify

errorCases.message: reason_code is required to record a breach
errorCases.when: no cause is given. A breach with no cause cannot be aggregated, so the report cannot say what is going wrong.

errorCases.message: recovery_action is required to record a breach
errorCases.when: no customer recovery is recorded. SOP §04 requires an action taken for the customer, not merely an internal explanation.

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, empty, or uses a scheme other than Bearer.

errorCases.message: Session token is invalid or expired
errorCases.when: a Bearer token was presented but does not verify.
